items.proposedAnswer: Enzymes are biological catalysts, mostly proteins, that speed up chemical reactions in living organisms without being used up. Examples: amylase, pepsin, catalase.
keyPoints: Speed up reactions without being consumed

items.q: What are essential amino acids? Why must they be supplied in the diet?
items.proposedAnswer: Essential amino acids are those that the human body cannot synthesise in sufficient amounts, so they must be obtained from food. Without them the body cannot make all the proteins it needs.

items.q: What is photorespiration and why is it considered a wasteful process?
items.proposedAnswer: In photorespiration RuBisCO combines RuBP with oxygen instead of CO₂, so carbon is lost as CO₂ without making sugar. It also does not produce ATP or NADPH but uses energy, so it reduces the efficiency of photosynthesis in C₃ plants.
keyPoints: RuBisCO acts on O₂ instead of CO₂

items.q: Why does the narrowing of arteries by fatty deposits (atherosclerosis) tend to raise blood pressure?
items.proposedAnswer: Deposits such as cholesterol plaques narrow the lumen of the arteries and make them less elastic, so there is more resistance to blood flow. The heart has to pump harder to push the blood through, so the pressure rises.
keyPoints: Heart pumps harder, so blood pressure increases

items.proposedAnswer: The block is in equilibrium, so friction balances the component of weight along the incline: f = mg sin 30° = 5 × 10 × 0.5 = 25 N, directed up the incline.
